mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% over a 6-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 4.0 for 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when RSAFS declines for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% signals an acceleration in economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when INDPRO > 12-month MA +2% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) over a 3-month window signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 6-month window signals a restrictive monetary stance coinciding with falling inflation, which increases discount rates but reduces inflation risk premia, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls for 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% signals an acceleration in residential investment, which boosts construction-related earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when HOUST > 12-month MA +5% for 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% over a 6-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 4.0 for 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).
